hints: Look left to right on the x-axis (partial pressure of oxygen). Which animal's curve rises to high saturation first, at the lowest partial pressure?
Remember the golden rule: a curve shifted to the left means haemoglobin loads oxygen easily at low pressure, so high affinity. A curve shifted to the right means low affinity.
walkthrough:
**Observe the positions of the curves**

Look carefully at the three curves. Animal 1 (dotted line) is furthest to the left. It reaches almost 100% saturation at a much lower partial pressure of oxygen than animal 2.

Animal 3 (dashed line) is furthest to the right.

**Apply the left-shift rule**

Think like this: if haemoglobin grabs oxygen even when there is very little oxygen around, it must love oxygen a lot.

So: left shift = higher affinity, loads easily. Right shift = lower affinity, needs higher pressure to load and unloads more easily.

**Compare animal 1 and animal 2**

Since animal 1 is to the left of animal 2, animal 1 loads oxygen at a lower partial pressure. That tells us animal 1 has the higher affinity haemoglobin.

We cannot tell respiration rate from this graph alone, so we choose the affinity conclusion.

options.A: Correct. Animal 1 curve is left-shifted compared to animal 2, so it saturates at lower partial pressure, showing higher affinity for oxygen.
options.B: Incorrect. Animal 3 curve is to the right of animal 2, so it needs higher pressure to saturate, showing lower affinity, not higher.
options.C: Incorrect. The graph shows affinity (position of curve), not respiration rate, so no conclusion about lower respiration rate can be made.
options.D: Incorrect. The graph shows affinity, not respiration rate, so no conclusion about higher respiration rate can be made.
